steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ensemble performance assesses your ability to LISTEN and RESPOND to other musicians — not just play your part accurately.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Balance means adjusting your volume so each part is heard appropriately; tuning means matching pitch with others continuously.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Following a leader (conductor or lead player) requires watching for cues, tempo changes and dynamic adjustments in real time.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Chamber music (string quartet, wind quintet) demands the highest level of ensemble skill — every player must lead and follow simultaneously.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how ensemble performance are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use ensemble performance. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use ensemble performance in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how ensemble performance are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language. | A practical application showing understanding of how ensemble performance can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
